subject.title: Fork-per-issue from one warmed repo box

question: Should Clownfish own a warmed snapshot-fork workspace lifecycle, consume a shared Mitos/Crabbox lease primitive, or continue relying on ordinary ephemeral checkouts and caches?
rationale: The choice changes Clownfish's infrastructure boundary and must define credential isolation, repository revision freshness, cache ownership, cleanup guarantees, fallback behavior, and acceptable backend coupling before implementation.

options.title: Define a lease interface
options.body: Adopt a backend-neutral opt-in workspace lease contract, validate it with one provider and measured canaries, and retain the existing checkout path as fallback.

options.title: Integrate one backend directly
options.body: Couple Clownfish to Mitos or Crabbox now, accepting a narrower deployment model in exchange for a faster initial implementation.

options.title: Keep current provisioning
options.body: Treat existing runner and package-store caching as sufficient and close the proposal without adding a workspace-pool architecture.

recommendation.title: Define a lease interface
recommendation.body: Adopt a backend-neutral opt-in workspace lease contract, validate it with one provider and measured canaries, and retain the existing checkout path as fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the adjacent target-checkout, execution, fan-out, and preflight paths that the decision would reshape.
